translation:
Here begins the holy Aarti ||8||

1. Parabrahma, Padmanabh, Purushottam -- he stands in no lineage. Hari the unmanifest, Govind, is my thought. Take care of us, Shripati, our Lord.

2. Hari is four-armed and dark of hue, the beautiful bearer of the Sharang bow. Hari is the lovely King of Vaikunth, Damodar who destroys sin.

3. Hari is stainless and formless; let us worship that spotless Purush (Person). Let us sing of Hari, the King of Dwarka, dark-hued and beautiful.

4. Serve Hari, the all-capable essence, whose farther limit no one can reach. That same Hari is imperishable; the Lord grants a dwelling in Vaikunth.

5. Hari is Madhav, Mukund, Murari -- the beautiful great God. Hari is the giver of bhakti (devotion) and mukti (liberation); Narayan is stainless.

6. Ever the bearer of the Sharang bow, of gracious discernment; Kanhaiya who is beyond, the very Self. [unclear] -- the three worlds writhe in longing for you to carry them across.

7. The poor soul is infatuated within its own imaginings; in the Kali age the soul is struck down. Without Hari it finds not a moment's breath; [unclear] -- the Lord, bearer of the Sharang bow.

8. Ever is there eagerness in the Vaishnav's heart, joy surging through the body. Welcome, King Parabrahma! The Beloved has come to dwell among the Vaishnav folk.

9. Hari's cry of victory has spread everywhere; sweet indeed is the essential word now. Faith in Hari has entered the mind; the nooses of the four sources of birth are loosed.

10. Father, in home after home there is now the dwelling of Vaikunth; your servants make their plea. Welcome, King Parabrahma -- the saints have served the all-capable Lord.

Here the holy Aarti is complete ||8||
